nodes.name: Sulfuration of stainless steel mesh
nodes.procedure: FeCl3.6H2O (3.5 g) and Na2S2O3.5H2O (0.15 g) were dissolved in 50 mL deionized water. And then a piece of stainless steel mesh (4 cm × 2 cm) was immersed in the aqueous solution at ambient temperature (20 - 30°C) for 30 min. The stainless steel mesh was washed several times with water to obtain MS/SS.
nodes.source_text: FeCl3.6H2O (3.5 g) and Na2S2O3.5H2O (0.15 g) were dissolved in 50 mL deionized water... washed several times with water to obtain MS/SS.

nodes.name: Large-scale sulfuration
nodes.procedure: A large-area MS/SS was prepared by immersing a piece of stainless steel mesh (1 m × 1 m) into 25 L of aqueous solution containing FeCl3.6H2O (2.4 kg) and Na2S2O3.5H2O (75 g) at ambient temperature for 10 min.
nodes.source_text: a large-area MS/SS was prepared by immersing a piece of stainless steel mesh (1 m × 1 m) into 25 L of aqueous solution containing FeCl3.6H2O (2.4 kg) and Na2S2O3.5H2O (75 g) at ambient temperature for 10 min.

nodes.source_text: LSV polarization curves in Fig. 2a show a redox peak around 1.4 V of MS/SS... nodes.description: OER performance comparison in lab-scale three-electrode system in 30% KOH
nodes.source_text: MS/SS has a much better OER activity than that of the SS; for instance, MS/SS displays a geometric current density of 90 mA cm_{geo}^{-2} at 1.53 V, which is about 7.2 times higher than that in the presence of SS. In addition, both MS/SS and SS electrodes display a Tafel slope close to 40 mV dec^{-1} ... MS/SS gives a higher surface area (18.7 cm²) than SS (8.9 cm²)

nodes.description: OER stability in simulated industrial conditions
nodes.source_text: MS/SS electrode can maintain its electrocatalytic activity unchanged for more than 600 h (Fig. S11) in a simulated industrial condition (80 °C in 30% KOH solution).

nodes.description: Industrial alkaline electrolyzer performance (400 cm² anode vs Raney Ni cathode)
nodes.source_text: The MS/SS electrode (≈400 cm²) was integrated into an industrial-scale electrolyzer as anode for OER... operating in 30% KOH electrolyte at 80 °C. ... the MS/SS-based electrolyzer was measured by stepping the current density from 50 mA cm^{-2} (1.55 V) to 310 mA cm^{-2} (2.08 V). ... provides a total steady operation for >120 h at current density of c.a. 300 mA cm^{-2} (2.0 V) under the start/stop conditions.

nodes.description: Industrial alkaline electrolyzer performance comparison (anode and cathode)
nodes.source_text: For comparison, the electrolyzers with Raney nickel electrodes as both anode and cathode were also tested. As shown in Fig. 4c, the MS/SS-based electrolyzer was measured by stepping the current density from 50 mA cm^{-2} (1.55 V) to 310 mA cm^{-2} (2.08 V). The required voltages are generally lower than those of Raney nickel-based electrolyzer

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of MS/SS and SS present the same diffraction peaks assigned to metallic nickel/iron.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD patterns of MS/SS and SS (Fig. S4) present the same diffraction peaks that are assigned to metallic nickel/iron.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM image shows MS/SS retains the mesh-connected structure but its surface is seriously cracked and become very rough because of chemical corrosion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM image shows that SS has a mesh-connected structure with a smooth surface (Fig. S3). By comparison, MS/SS retains the mesh-connected structure (Fig. 1c), but its surface is seriously cracked and become very rough because of chemical corrosion.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM image shows no lattice fringes of MS/SS, confirming the amorphous nature. SAED pattern exhibits a broad diffused halo ring.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM image shows no lattice fringes of MS/SS, confirming the amorphous nature (Fig. S5). In addition, the amorphous nature of the MS/SS is also supported by the SAED pattern (Fig. S5, inset), which exhibits a broad diffused halo ring.

nodes.characterization_summary: MS/SS presents Raman characteristic peaks at 310, 370, and 460 cm⁻¹, suggesting the formation of sulfide phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The MS/SS presents Raman characteristic peaks at 310, 370, and 460 cm⁻¹, suggesting the formation of sulfide phases (Fig. S6).

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping analysis reveals that the Fe, Ni, Cr, S and O elements are homogeneously distributed over the surface layers of MS/SS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Further elemental mapping analysis (Fig. 1d) reveals that the Fe, Ni, Cr, S and O elements are homogeneously distributed over the surface layers of MS/SS.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution S 2p XPS spectrum shows peaks at 163.0 eV and 164.4 eV confirming M-S bonding, and 168.9 eV for oxidized sulfur species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the high-resolution S 2p XPS spectrum (Fig. 1e), the peaks at 163.0 eV and 164.4 eV confirm the bonding of sulfur and metal atoms, while the peak at 168.9 eV is assigned to oxidized sulfur species because of surface oxidation.

nodes.characterization_summary: MS/SS gives electrochemical double layer capacitance Cdl corresponding to ECSA of 18.7 cm².
nodes.evidence_snippet: MS/SS gives a higher surface area (18.7 cm²) than SS (8.9 cm²), demonstrating that the corrosion-induced surface roughening can lead to a considerable increase of ECSA value.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows charge transfer resistance Rct = 0.12 Ω for MS/SS electrode.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Nyquist plots from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) measurements (Fig. 2c) also reveal that the electron transfer process in MS/SS electrode (charge transfer resistance Rct = 0.12 Ω) is faster than that in SS electrode (Rct = 0.76 Ω).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman during OER shows transformation from sulfide phases (peaks at 310, 370, 460 cm⁻¹) to γ-NiOOH (peaks at 477, 558 cm⁻¹) confirming γ-(Ni,Fe)OOH as active phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: When the potential is higher than 1.36 V (to at least 1.43 V), Raman signal no longer alters in position, and two strong Raman bands at 477 and 558 cm⁻¹ are ascribed to γ-NiOOH. These results overall demonstrate that γ-(Ni,Fe)OOH serves as active phase for OER.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES quantifies leached S, Fe, Cr, Ni ions during 10h OER stability test, showing higher dissolution of S and Cr.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The dissolutions of the four ions increase at the first two hours and then become nearly stable. The total leached concentrations of S and Cr ions are much higher than those of Fe and Ni cations.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER XPS shows no Cr and S signals on surface. Ni 2p and Fe 2p indicate Ni²⁺ and Fe³⁺ states with Ni:Fe ~2:1. O 1s deconvoluted to M-O (530.7 eV), M-OH (531.5 eV), H₂O (532.5 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: No Cr and S signals are observed in the XPS spectra on the surface of MS/SS after OER (Fig. S15a,b), suggesting that all Cr and S atoms are leached from the catalyst surface. Ni 2p and Fe 2p XPS spectra (Fig. S15c,d) show that both Ni and Fe maintain oxidized states (i.e., Ni²⁺ and Fe³⁺)... The O 1 s spectrum (Fig. 5b) can be deconvoluted into three peaks, including M-O (530.7 eV), M-OH (531.5 eV) and adsorbed water (532.5 eV).
